page.layout: One column of running text filling the page. Below the last full line, at the right, one catchword ("cedi"). No running head, no page number, no margin notes.

main_text.p: quàm ab his penes quos est plena & legitima de ejusmodi rebus statuendi potestas, personæ ipsorum judicio non inidoneæ, nulla intercedente pravâ ambitione, dolo, malisve artibus, de-signatio.Pervicit itaque omnia impedimenta, omnia objectamenta diluit, duplex illa parendi necessitas, voluntati Regiæ, divinæ vocationi. Quò mihi paratiorem apud omnes bonos, apud omnes æquos rerum æstimatores excu-sationem fore confida, si (quod indubiè futurum prospicio) in obeundo hoc tàm illustri tàm arduo munere, nec vo-tis meis, nec vestræ expectationi satis-facerem.Dabo tamen operam officio utcunque ut satisfaciam meo: & sane, ut aliquid saltem de me fidenter dicam, spero me aliqua ex parte satisfacturum: illud si concedatis, quod omnino con-

page.notes: "Quò" is underlined in the print. "excu-sationem" (the second line of the paragraph's ending word) is read as "sationem"; the long s makes the initial letter look like f. "confida," is read with a final comma and a doubtful "a" ([?] not marked because it is legible at this scan). The ampersand "&" is the printed ornate form. Accents on "tàm", "pravâ", "indubiè" and "Quò" are as printed. Page is mid-sentence at the top and ends mid-sentence with a catchword.
